citation: Quaranta, C. (2024). In the mood for Heideggerian boredom? Film viewership as being-in-the-world. Film-Philosophy, 28(1), 31-46. https://doi.org/10.3366/film.2024.0253
thesis: Loht's (2017) viewing-Dasein argument -- that film viewing is a bidirectional disclosedness extending being-in-the-world, structured through Mitsein -- treats boredom only in passing; deepening that argument via Heidegger's Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics (rather than Being and Time, which Loht favors) shows profound boredom to be a privileged mood for disclosing characters' and spectators' being-in a film world, demonstrated through a close reading of Hamaguchi's Drive My Car (2021).

sections.title: Abstract/Introduction
sections.summary: Frames the engagement with Loht's Phenomenology of Film (2017), diagnoses the FCM-shaped gap in his treatment of boredom (he relies on Being and Time and on fear as his exemplary mood), previews the Drive My Car case study.

sections.title: Worldhood, Moods, Understanding
sections.summary: Rehearses Heidegger's being-in-the-world (attunement/Befindlichkeit, understanding/Verstehen, discourse/Rede), Mitsein, mood (Stimmung) as ontic manifestation of attunement, fundamental moods (Grundstimmungen) vs. ordinary moods, thrownness (Geworfenheit), and the three forms of boredom, closing on profound boredom as authentic disclosure of finitude via originary temporality.

sections.title: Film Viewership as Being-in-the-(Cinematic-)World
sections.summary: Expounds Loht's bidirectional-disclosedness thesis (viewer discloses the film / film discloses to viewer) and introduces 'aesthetics of mood' (after Sinnerbrink 2012) as the mechanism by which a film's aesthetic choices arouse moods disclosing a meaningful cinematic world; stresses moods are neither purely subjective nor objective.

sections.title: Temporal Entrancement in Drive My Car
sections.summary: Sustained close reading: silence and noise as time-dilating devices, fixed shots and minimal movement, verbal/visual repetition, the Hokkaido car-drive sequence, the self-disclosive dialogue (Kafuku's confession) it enables, and the climactic two-hands shot read via Loht's Heidegger-on-artworks/Rashomon discussion as cinematic disclosure of being.

sections.title: Heideggerian Film-Philosophy(?)
sections.summary: Closes with reservations about a fully Heideggerian film-philosophy: rigidity, exclusion of the body/ethics, over-reliance on Malick/Antonioni, neglect of Heidegger's own critique of film; contrasts favorably (but only partially) with the embodied film-phenomenology tradition (Sobchack, Barker, Marks).

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: central organizing construct; paraphrased from FCM and extended to film spectatorship as the mood disclosing shared finitude in a cinematic world

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: defined briefly, definitional contrast only, not independently applied to cinema

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: defined briefly, definitional contrast only, not independently applied to cinema

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: operative throughout the Drive My Car reading via the author's own coinage 'temporal entrancement'; silence, repetition, fixed shots read as producing time-drag

constructs.label: monotony/meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: named at the essay's close as the 'boresome' character of contemporary everydayness, a busyness that turns away from the burden of existence

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: not named or discussed anywhere in the text

constructs.label: boredom proneness
constructs.treatment: not named or discussed; not a psychological/dispositional reading

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: not framed in these psychological terms; the FCM forms are existential-ontological, not situational/dispositional in the empirical sense

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: not engaged; the reading is disclosure-ontological throughout, in unaddressed tension with functional accounts (cf. bor-sec-25/26)

measures.label: (none operationalized)
measures.note: purely hermeneutic/textual-and-filmic close-reading method; no EEG, gaze/pupillometry, self-report scale, behavioral, predictive-processing, or ML construct appears anywhere in the source

readings.summary: Transplants FCM's third-form conclusion (profound boredom as disclosure, via a crisis of everyday meaning, of Dasein's groundless finitude) onto film-viewership via Loht's Mitsein-based bridge; does not walk through FCM's own structural apparatus (Leergelassenheit/Hingehaltenheit transformation, Gebanntheit, Augenblick) -- 'temporal entrancement' is the author's own cinematic gloss, not a citation of Heidegger's Gebanntheit.
Cites the first form's trapping of Dasein in an 'inauthentic past, present and future' as contrastive backdrop for the third form's depth.
Names the second form (Sichlangweilen bei etwas) in passing, no extended engagement.

concepts.gloss: being-with; ontological basis for Loht's shared cinematic world regardless of characters' actual presence
ontic manifestation of attunement (Befindlichkeit); disclosive of the world
one of three equiprimordial structures of being-in (with understanding and discourse)
distinguished from ordinary moods as responsible for authentically assuming the burden of thrownness
the burdensome 'that it is and has to be' of finite existence, revealed in fundamental mood
becoming bored by a determinate entity or situation
being bored with something while outwardly engaged

concepts.term: tiefe Langeweile / es ist einem langweilig (3rd form)
concepts.gloss: profound, impersonal boredom in which time itself bores 'one'
aesthetic choices that arouse suitable moods to open up a meaningful cinematic world (after Sinnerbrink 2012)
Quaranta's own cinematic gloss for the aesthetic production of time-drag; not a direct citation of Heidegger's Gebanntheit

tensions: profound-boredom-is-boredom vs. profound-boredom-is-a-distinct-existential-mood (Elpidorou & Freeman's skeptical thesis is footnoted, p.35, but never engaged -- this reading sits unreflectively on the Heideggerian-orthodox side)

rigid single-philosophy Heideggerian film approach vs. flexible embodied film-phenomenology tradition (explicitly conceded in the author's own favor of the latter's productivity, pp.43-44, while still defending a limited Heideggerian contribution)
phenomenological-disclosure account of boredom (this source) vs. functional/regulatory account of boredom (bor-sec-25/26, Elpidorou) -- the two paradigms are never brought into contact in this text
